name: Magic Internet Money
oneLiner: MIM is Abracadabra's CDP-style stablecoin minted against interest-bearing tokens and crypto collateral in cauldron vaults, with automatic liquidations.
collateral: Interest-bearing tokens and crypto collateral deposited into active Abracadabra cauldrons, currently concentrated in yvDAI and WBTC with smaller yvWETH/WETH positions
pegMechanism: CDP-style cauldrons with overcollateralization and automatic liquidations (4% liquidation fee); borrowers are incentivized to buy MIM below $1 to repay debt; 0.5% borrow/interest fees accrue to sSPELL stakers and governance treasury

oracleRisk.summary: Abracadabra Cauldrons use per-market external oracles connected to each market, but reviewed docs do not prove stronger failover controls.

branchApplicability.reviewer: Codex Safety Score V9 small-1-free oracle review
branchApplicability.rationale: Abracadabra documents one oracle per Cauldron and a liquidation path for undercollateralized positions, but the reviewed primary sources do not provide the complete current debt-bearing Cauldron inventory, deployed oracle and fallback configuration, branch parameters, or system-level bad-debt and shutdown coverage.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The verified MIM token source exposes owner-controlled mint functions and the owner is a 5-of-11 Safe. The reviewed cauldron and reserve metadata also include stablecoin collateral such as DAI, so upstream issuer freeze exposure is retained. The sources do not establish one direct holder-freeze implementation across MIM's material deployments, so no direct blacklist boolean is asserted.
blacklistabilityReview.reviewer: SONG Safety Score V9 access review

mintAuthority.summary: The Ethereum MIM contract exposes owner-controlled mint functions. Owner is a 5/11 Safe with no modules or guard detected.

mintIncidents.summary: Abracadabra cauldron borrow logic was exploited to enable unauthorized MIM borrowing, turning the stablecoin mint/borrow route into bad debt.

Flawed collateral accounting in Abracadabra's GMX-integrated gmCauldrons left phantom collateral after failed deposit orders and self-liquidation, letting the attacker borrow about 13.4M MIM (~$13M in ETH) against collateral the system failed to remove.

A cook() action-sequencing flaw in deprecated CauldronV4 contracts reset the solvency-check flag, letting attackers borrow about 1.79M MIM with no collateral; the DAO bought back the supply to defend the peg.

controls.label: MIM owner Safe
controls.evidence: MIM.owner() returns this Safe. Safe Transaction Service returned threshold 5 with 11 current owners, no modules, and nonce 260; Sourcify ABI for MagicInternetMoneyV1 exposes mint and mintToBentoBox.

review.evidence: Ethereum MIM owner reads and Sourcify ABI identify a 5/11 Safe owner with direct owner-controlled mint functions on the token. Re-verified by direct chain reads at Ethereum block 25575152 on 2026-07-20: MIM 0x99d8a9c45b2eca8864373a26d1459e3dff1e17f3 owner() returns Safe 0x5f0DeE98360d8200b20812e174d139A1a633EDd2, which returns getThreshold()=5 over the same eleven owners, an empty getModulesPaginated array, a zero guard slot, and Safe 1.3.0 masterCopy 0xd9db270c1b5e3bd161e8c8503c55ceabee709552. Economic-control adjudication: the token owner Safe holds unconditional mint and mintToBentoBox entry points with no on-chain cap, no timelock, and no independent bound, so the mint cap is economically unbounded. There is no supply-versus-reserve attestation of any cadence and the token-level owner mint means outstanding MIM cannot be reconciled to cauldron collateral from on-chain reads alone, so reconciliation stays unknown, and no financial regulator supervises Abracadabra. The mint surface is only enumerated on Ethereum: this profile records a single control for an asset deployed across fourteen chains, so the review remains unresolved rather than scoreable.
review.reviewer: Codex mint-authority top100 batch-c; Claude V9 Phase 3 curation lane cur-14 (economic-control fields, 2026-07-20)
unresolvedQuestions: Confirm whether current protocol cauldrons rely on owner minting directly or only through approved borrowing modules; the token-level owner path is still a direct mint surface.

Enumerate the mint-capable surface on the thirteen non-Ethereum MIM deployments (Arbitrum, Avalanche, Fantom, BSC, Optimism, Polygon, Kava, Blast, Moonriver, Nibiru, Base, Linea) — no owner, minter role, or bridge mint controller has been read on any of them.
Establish whether the 5-of-11 owner Safe is subject to any off-chain governance constraint; no timelock, guard, or module was detected on-chain at block 25575152.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Abracadabra documents MIM Beaming as LayerZero OFT-powered omnichain transfers, but on-chain reads on 2026-07-20 confirm the twelve long-standing MIM deployments are plain owner-gated tokens whose owners are Abracadabra team Safes (signer sets shared with the Ethereum 5/11 Safe), i.e. issuer-native burn-mint per chain; only the newer Berachain deployment is a LayerZero OFT representation.

notices.title: Recurring cauldron exploit history
notices.message: Abracadabra/MIM has suffered three material cauldron-related incidents since January 2024: a January 2024 borrow-logic exploit, a March 2025 gmCauldron collateral-accounting exploit, and an October 2025 deprecated CauldronV4 sequencing exploit. Treat cauldron implementation and deprecation risk as recurring protocol risk.

notices.title: Severe depeg and unexplained DAO treasury transfers
notices.message: MIM remained severely depegged as of July 15, 2026. On July 14, Abracadabra-controlled Ethereum and Arbitrum Safes moved roughly $8.3M of treasury assets at then-current prices, including about 2,142 ETH/WETH to a Binance-tagged deposit address and about $4.30M of USDC/USDT to an unlabeled address that immediately forwarded the funds. The Ethereum Safe had also sold 500,000 MIM into Curve on June 8 and 11 for about $489,000. Pharos found no public explanation from Abracadabra as of July 15. These facts do not establish theft, and treasury assets are not MIM's direct cauldron collateral, but the transfers reduce the DAO's transparent onchain treasury backstop while destination control remains unknown.
